          # in by orange-book's `appendices()` show rule (the .typ source

          - "B\\.\\s+Supplementary\\s+Data"

          - "See\\s+Tip\\s+B\\.1\\s+for\\s+the\\s+Appendix\\s+B\\s+tip"
          - "See\\s+Dinosaur\\s+B\\.1\\s+for\\s+the\\s+Appendix\\s+B\\s+dinosaur"

          - "\\(1\\.2\\)"
          - "\\(2\\.1\\)"
          - "\\(A\\.1\\)"
          - "As\\s+shown\\s+in\\s+Equation\\s+\\(1\\.1\\)\\s*,\\s+energy\\s+and\\s+mass"
          - "Newton.s\\s+second\\s+law\\s+\\(\\s*Equation\\s+\\(1\\.2\\)\\s*\\)"
          - "Use\\s+Equation\\s+\\(2\\.1\\)\\s+to\\s+solve\\s+quadratic\\s+equations"

          - "Lemma\\s+1\\.1.*Triangle\\s+Inequality"
          - "Theorem\\s+2\\.1.*Fundamental\\s+Theorem"
          - "Definition\\s+2\\.1.*Continuous"

          - "Recall\\s+Theorem\\s+1\\.1\\s+and\\s+Lemma\\s+1\\.1\\s+from\\s+Chapter\\s+1\\."
          # Critical: Appendix theorem should be A.1, not continuing from chapters
          - "Theorem\\s+A\\.1.*Example\\s+Appendix\\s+Theorem"
          # Critical: Appendix references to earlier chapter theorems should show original numbering
          # This tests the fix for ctheorems bug where cross-refs resolved at reference time
          - "Reference\\s+Theorem\\s+1\\.1\\s+from\\s+Chapter\\s+1\\.\\s+and\\s+Theorem\\s+2\\.1\\s+from\\s+Chapter\\s+2\\."
          - "Listing\\s+1\\.1.*Hello\\s+World"
          - "Listing\\s+1\\.2.*Fibonacci"
          - "Listing\\s+2\\.1.*Quicksort"
          - "Listing\\s+A\\.1.*Appendix\\s+Code\\s+Example"
          - "See\\s+Listing\\s+1\\.1\\s+for\\s+a\\s+simple\\s+Python\\s+example"
          - "Listing\\s+1\\.2.*uses\\s+recursion"
          - "See\\s+Listing\\s+2\\.1\\s+for\\s+an\\s+efficient\\s+sorting\\s+algorithm"
          - "See\\s+Listing\\s+A\\.1\\s+for\\s+an\\s+appendix\\s+code\\s+example"
          - "See\\s+Listing\\s+1\\.1\\s+and\\s+Listing\\s+1\\.2\\s+from\\s+Chapter\\s+1\\."
          # Bibliography aggregation tests - with citeproc, uses author-date format
          - "McCarthy,\\s+John.*1960.*Recursive\\s+Functions"
          - "Codd,\\s+Edgar\\s+F.*1970.*Relational\\s+Model"
          - "Lamport,\\s+Leslie.*1978.*Time,\\s+Clocks"
          # Inline citation tests - citeproc renders as Author (Year)
          - "Turing\\s+\\(1950\\)\\s+on\\s+machine\\s+intelligence"
          - "McCarthy\\s+\\(1960\\)\\s+inspired\\s+this\\s+classification"
          - "Codd\\s+\\(1970\\)\\s+informs\\s+our\\s+approach"
          - "Lamport\\s+\\(1978\\)\\s+for\\s+temporal\\s+considerations"
      # `chapter1.qmd`'s "Code Listings" section opens with a raw Typst
      # `#pagebreak()` (P8, 2026-09-29) so LISTING_BODY_ALIGN_TEST and the
      # Listing 1.1 figure (ALIGNTEST_MARKER) always start together at the
      # top of a fresh page — before that fix they straddled an ordinary
      # page break (the listing didn't fit in the remaining space on the
      # previous page), which this assertion's leftAligned relation can't
      # compare across (crates/quarto-test/src/assertions/pdf_text_position.rs:523-529,
      # "Cannot compare positions ... is on page N, ... is on page M").
      ensurePdfTextPositions:
        - # Code listings should be left-aligned with body text, not centered.
          # NOTE: Subject must be text at the START of a line because
          # ensurePdfTextPositions uses word positions, not semantic containers.
          - subject: "ALIGNTEST_MARKER"
            relation: leftAligned
            object: "LISTING_BODY_ALIGN_TEST"
            tolerance: 10  # 8pt inset from Skylighting block styling
      # The remaining 2 warnings are the embed gap — see the
      # `<fig-visualization>` comment above (`{{< embed >}}` unimplemented,
      # D6). bd-quarto-tests-metadata-markdown-3wsdzq4c's markdown-parsing
      # false positives are fixed (meta_annotations.rs's `_quarto.tests.**`
      # entry); this is back to the tightest check short of landing D6.
      printsMessage:
        - level: WARN
          regex: "Unknown shortcode"
        - level: WARN
          regex: "unresolved crossref `@fig-visualization`"
      noErrors: true
---

# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a test book for Typst output format.

## About this book

This book tests the basic Typst book rendering functionality in Quarto.
See @knuth84 for additional discussion of literate programming.
